item.title: Sample Page
item.dc:creator: Bdyculture
item.content:encoded:
This is an example page. It's different from a blog post because it will stay in one place and will show up in your site navigation (in most themes). Most people start with an About page that introduces them to potential site visitors. It might say something like this:

Hi there! I'm a bike messenger by day, aspiring actor by night, and this is my website. I live in Los Angeles, have a great dog named Jack, and I like piña coladas. (And gettin' caught in the rain.)

...or something like this:

The XYZ Doohickey Company was founded in 1971, and has been providing quality doohickeys to the public ever since. Located in Gotham City, XYZ employs over 2,000 people and does all kinds of awesome things for the Gotham community.

As a new WordPress user, you should go to your dashboard to delete this page and create new pages for your content. Have fun!

item.dc:creator: Bdyculture
item.content:encoded:
Who we are

Suggested text: Our website address is: http://bdyculture.test.

Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Suggested text: Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

1. About this Privacy Policy

BDYCULTURE, operated by Bdycorporation Pty Ltd, is committed to protecting the privacy of our patients, clients, referrers and website users.

We handle personal information in accordance with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), the Australian Privacy Principles and other applicable legal, professional and healthcare requirements.

2. Information We Collect

We may collect personal and sensitive information including:

  • name, date of birth, address, phone number and email address
  • health, medical, injury and disability information
  • referral information and clinical history
  • appointment and treatment information
  • Medicare, DVA, NDIS, WorkCover, CTP, private health and other funding information where relevant
  • payment and billing information
  • emergency contact details
  • correspondence, enquiries, feedback and complaints
  • information submitted through our website, referral forms or online booking systems.

We only collect information that is reasonably necessary for our functions and services.

3. How We Collect Information

We may collect information directly from you, from your authorised representative, or from third parties involved in your care or funding, including GPs, medical specialists, allied health professionals, hospitals, insurers, government agencies, NDIS participants and representatives, support coordinators and plan managers.

Information may be collected in person, by telephone, email, online forms, referral documents, our practice management system or other secure electronic systems.

4. How We Use and Disclose Information

We may use or disclose your information for purposes including:

  • providing allied health, rehabilitation and related services
  • assessing, planning, delivering and reviewing your care
  • communicating with you and other members of your healthcare team
  • managing appointments, referrals and clinical records
  • processing payments, claims and funding
  • meeting Medicare, DVA, NDIS, WorkCover, CTP or other funding requirements where applicable
  • responding to enquiries, feedback or complaints
  • managing our clinic and improving our services
  • complying with legal, regulatory, professional and insurance obligations.

We will not sell your personal information.

5. Marketing Communications

Where you have consented, we may contact you about clinic updates, services, educational information or other relevant communications.

You may opt out of marketing communications at any time. Opting out of marketing communications will not prevent us from contacting you about your healthcare, appointments or other necessary service-related matters.

6. Storage and Security

We take reasonable steps to protect personal and health information from misuse, interference, loss, unauthorised access, modification or disclosure.

Information may be stored in secure electronic systems, cloud services and, where required, physical records. We use service providers and technology systems to support clinical care, administration, communication, website operation and business functions.

We retain information for periods required by applicable laws, professional standards, funding requirements and clinical obligations.

7. Overseas Storage and Service Providers

Some technology and service providers used by BDYCULTURE may store, process or access information outside Australia. Where applicable, we take reasonable steps to ensure personal information is handled in accordance with Australian privacy requirements.

We will update this policy where practicable to reflect material changes to the locations in which information is processed or stored.

8. Website, Cookies and Analytics

Our website may use cookies and analytics technologies to understand website use, improve performance and measure the effectiveness of our communications and marketing.

Information collected through these technologies may include device information, browser information, pages visited and general website interaction data.

9. Accessing or Correcting Your Information

You may request access to personal information we hold about you or ask us to correct information that is inaccurate, incomplete or out of date.

Requests can be made using the contact details below. In some circumstances, access may be limited where permitted or required by law.

10. Privacy Complaints

If you have concerns about how BDYCULTURE has handled your personal information, please contact us so we can investigate and respond.

If you are not satisfied with our response, you may also contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC).

Evidence-based Physiotherapy for pain, injury, post-operative recovery and movement limitations, supported by progressive rehabilitation in our dedicated clinic and exercise environment.
Physiotherapy that starts with understanding how you move.

Physiotherapy at BDYCULTURE begins with a conversation. Your physiotherapist wants to know what has changed, what you can no longer do comfortably and what you would like to get back to. They then assess how you move, explain what they find in plain language and agree a plan with you before treatment begins.

Treatment can include hands-on techniques, guided movement, education and a progressive exercise program. Because our Chermside clinic includes a dedicated rehabilitation and exercise space, care can move from symptom management towards strength, conditioning and long-term physical capacity without sending you elsewhere to find the right equipment.

Physiotherapy is one of four allied health services at the clinic, alongside exercise physiology, occupational therapy and clinical Pilates. If your needs change, the practitioners involved in your care work from the same building and can stay across your goals.

Appointments can be booked online through Nookal in a couple of minutes, or you can call the clinic on 07 3073 1616. If you are referred by a GP, specialist, insurer or case manager, bring any referral details and reports with you.

Our Physiotherapists assess the factors contributing to pain, injury and movement limitations, then develop an individual treatment and rehabilitation plan focused on restoring function and helping you move with confidence.
Assessment and management of muscle, joint and soft-tissue pain, including what may be contributing to it and how it affects your day.
Assessment, treatment and guided exercise for back and neck pain, with advice on movement and activity.

Assessment and a rehabilitation plan for conditions affecting joints, muscles and tendons.
Structured rehabilitation after surgery to rebuild movement, strength and confidence, alongside your surgeon’s guidance.

You do not need to wait until it gets worse.

Many people put off seeing a physiotherapist because they hope a problem will settle on its own. Sometimes it does, but early advice can make it clearer what is safe to keep doing and what to change. If something has been bothering you for more than a few days, has returned repeatedly, or is limiting work, sport or sleep, it is reasonable to get it assessed.

Consider booking if you:

  • have pain that is not settling, or that keeps coming back
  • are recovering from surgery and want structured rehabilitation
  • have been injured at work or in a motor vehicle accident and hold a claim
  • feel stiff, weak or unsteady and are unsure why
  • want a safe plan for returning to exercise after an injury

If you experience sudden severe symptoms, chest pain, or loss of function after an accident, seek urgent medical help or call 07 3073 1616. This page is general information and is not a substitute for individual health advice.
Can’t see yours? Call 07 3073 1616 or send us a message.
Do I need a referral to see a Physiotherapist?
No referral is required for private Physiotherapy appointments. Some funded or insurance pathways may require a referral, claim approval or other documentation.
What should I expect at my first Physiotherapy appointment?
Your Physiotherapist will discuss your symptoms, medical history and goals, assess your movement and function, explain the findings and develop an individual treatment and rehabilitation plan.
What should I bring to my appointment?
Bring any relevant referrals, imaging, reports or claim information, and wear comfortable clothing that allows the affected area to be assessed where appropriate.

Yes. Where appropriate, Physiotherapy may include individually prescribed exercise in our dedicated rehabilitation and exercise environment to improve strength, mobility, function and confidence as part of your rehabilitation plan.

Evidence-based exercise physiology for chronic conditions, injury rehabilitation, strength, mobility and long-term health, delivered within our dedicated rehabilitation and exercise environment.
Exercise, prescribed and supervised like a treatment.

Exercise physiology uses carefully planned, supervised exercise as the treatment. At BDYCULTURE, your exercise physiologist starts by understanding your health history, your current capacity and what you want to be able to do. They then design a program around you, rather than handing over a generic routine.

Sessions take place in the clinic’s dedicated rehabilitation and exercise space, which sits alongside our consulting rooms. That means your exercise physiologist can explain what you are doing and why, adjust loads and movements on the spot, and progress your program as your capacity builds.

Exercise physiology is often used for chronic conditions, for rehabilitation after injury, and for building strength, mobility and long-term health. It sits naturally alongside physiotherapy, occupational therapy and clinical Pilates, and because these practitioners work from the same clinic, your goals can stay consistent across your care.

You can book online through Nookal in a couple of minutes, or call 07 3073 1616. If a GP, specialist, insurer or case manager has referred you, bring the referral details and any reports to your first appointment.

Exercise physiology is for more than athletes.

Many people assume exercise physiology is only for sport. In practice, it is used by people of many ages and abilities, particularly where exercise needs to be planned carefully around health history, pain or confidence. If you have been told to “get more active” but are not sure where to start, a supervised program can take the guesswork out of it.

You might consider exercise physiology if you:

  • are managing a chronic condition and want a safe plan for exercise
  • are recovering from an injury and want to rebuild strength
  • want help to improve strength, mobility or general fitness
  • have a GP-supported chronic condition plan, or a funded claim or plan
  • feel unsure how hard to push and want clear guidance

Occupational Therapy focused on improving independence, safety and participation in everyday activities, with assessment and practical strategies tailored to your individual needs and goals.
Occupational therapy starts with what matters in your day.

In occupational therapy, “occupation” simply means the everyday things you need, want or are expected to do: getting ready in the morning, working, caring for others, cooking, getting around, enjoying hobbies. Your occupational therapist looks at what makes those activities harder than they should be and works with you on practical ways to change that.

An assessment may consider your physical abilities, your environment and your routines, as well as what you want to achieve. From there, your therapist agrees a plan with you, which might include strategies, practice, adjustments to how tasks are done, or recommendations about equipment and supports.

Occupational therapy at BDYCULTURE sits alongside physiotherapy, exercise physiology and clinical Pilates in the same Chermside clinic. If your plan includes strength, conditioning or movement work, those practitioners are close by and can stay across your goals.

Clinical Pilates combines individually prescribed Pilates-based exercise with rehabilitation principles to improve strength, movement, control and physical capacity in a supervised clinical environment.

Clinical Pilates uses Pilates-based exercise within a rehabilitation setting. At BDYCULTURE it is delivered by our Physiotherapists and Accredited Exercise Physiologists, so each session is shaped by an assessment of you rather than a one-size-fits-all class format.

Your practitioner begins by understanding your history, your goals and how you move. They then select and adapt exercises to support rehabilitation, strength, movement and physical capacity, explaining the purpose of each one so you understand what you are working on and why.

Because clinical Pilates is part of the same Chermside clinic as physiotherapy, exercise physiology and occupational therapy, it can sit comfortably within a broader plan. For some people it follows treatment; for others it runs alongside it, supported by the clinic’s rehabilitation and exercise space.

You can book online through Nookal, call 07 3073 1616, or send an enquiry. If you have been referred, bring the details and any reports to your first appointment. Clinical Pilates is available as one-to-one private sessions or small-group sessions, using reformer, mat and other Pilates-based exercises.

How clinical Pilates differs from a general class.

General Pilates classes can be a great way to stay active, but they are usually designed for a group. Clinical Pilates is different because the person guiding you is a qualified clinician who has assessed you, and the exercises are chosen and modified around your history and goals.

You might consider clinical Pilates if you:

  • want movement-based rehabilitation with close professional guidance
  • are building strength and control after an injury or procedure
  • prefer an individualised approach to a group class
  • want exercise to complement physiotherapy or exercise physiology
  • hold a funded claim or plan that includes clinical Pilates
